answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs bind identity to hardware cost. Each agent computes a proof demanding sustained RAM per head, making copper and silicon expenditure for N clones scale linearly while honest operators amortize one rig. The protocol kernel verifies every attestation carries a fresh sequential proof and Falcon signature, binding identity to memory work and post-quantum cryptography. Attacker needs N separate RAM modules because proofs cannot be parallelized or outsourced to cloud GPUs. Network enforces via on-chain verification.
